problem:
Expressed in **ascending order** in radians, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{3}{5},$ for $-\pi <x\le \pi ,$  are

$x≈$
{{field-1}}$,\,x≈$
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{3}{5})=0.643\,501…≈0.6435\end{aligned}
$$

Since $0.6435$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=0.6435.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=0.6435.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=0.6435.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13992768/assets/962545fd6fa64e121a99eb8bf684484e4b457dbd4defedd7c07ae88fd47cac6e.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -0.6435 \\  & ≈2.4981.\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions are 

$$
x≈0.6,\,x≈2.5.
$$
